claims.claim: The canonical contract defines prospective Personal-First, Direct-Activation with personal-use rationale, same-TASK enablement, and no default pilot, effectiveness benchmark or second activation decision.

The policy separates functional Runtime verification and valid evidence from optional effectiveness evaluation, preserves minimum-sufficient-v1 and independent Reviewer/Publisher duties, and rejects default ceremonial rechecks.

The contract removes enterprise security ceremony for low-risk local upgrades while preserving credentials, source integrity, authenticated identity/provenance, currentness/CAS, mutation boundaries and irreversible/external-risk controls.

Both CAA documents distinguish optional study-specific gates from normal activation, retain evaluator implementation and study integrity rules, and leave CAA-05 unselected without a mandatory trial cohort.

One new prospective Human/Brain policy record specifies supersession boundaries. Every prior roadmap value remains unchanged, including the sole TASK-419 r2 NEXT; TASK-417/419/420 artifacts and lifecycle history remain untouched.

The committed change contains only the four permitted documents/planning files, uses a consistent activation boundary, preserves existing Brain Sync selection and authoring-policy data, and introduces no planner, router, workflow or optional-support ingress prerequisite.
